name: Mini RTL-SDR Dongle
one_line: USB-C RTL2832U+R860 SDR receiver, 100kHz-1.74GHz, in a CNC aluminum case with TCXO and switchable 5V bias tee.
why_notable: Compact, aluminum-housed RTL-SDR variant with bias tee and HF direct sampling not covered by the existing RTL-SDR Blog V4 entry.

name: RTL-SDR/LoRa/GPS/RTC hat for Raspberry Pi
one_line: Raspberry Pi HAT combining an RTL2832U+R860 SDR receiver, SX1262 LoRa radio, GPS/GNSS, and RTC on one board.
why_notable: All-in-one SDR/LoRa/GPS expansion board for turning a Raspberry Pi into a portable signal-monitoring platform.

name: Pwnagotchi Hat - UPS/GPS/AC WiFi/USB HUB/RTC all in one hat
one_line: Raspberry Pi Zero expansion board purpose-built for Pwnagotchi: dual-band AC WiFi with monitor mode/packet injection, GPS with PPS, UPS, USB hub and RTC.
why_notable: Dedicated hardware carrier for building a Pwnagotchi wardriving unit with GPS logging and battery runtime beyond the base project's typical hardware.

name: AC1200 USB-C WiFi Card (supports monitor mode)
one_line: MT7921AUN-based WiFi 6E/BT 5.2 M.2 card with monitor-mode support, sized to install inside the uConsole AIO board.
why_notable: Monitor-mode-capable WiFi 6E radio card sold specifically for pentest/wardriving builds, though it only fits inside the uConsole enclosure rather than standing alone.

name: uConsole AIO V2 (RTL-SDR/LoRa/GPS/RTC/USB Hub/USB 3.0/RJ45 Ethernet)
one_line: Expansion board for the ClockworkPi uConsole adding an RTL-SDR receiver, LoRa radio, GPS, RTC, and USB 3.0/RJ45 ports.
why_notable: Turns the uConsole handheld into a field SDR/LoRa/GPS platform via a single expansion board; pre-order item.

name: MalDuino 3
one_line: Arduino-based BadUSB keystroke injector with 128MB onboard storage for file exfiltration, dual USB-A/C, and 34 keyboard-locale support. Converted from GBP 35 at ~1.354 USD/GBP.
why_notable: Current-generation MalDuino model with built-in exfiltration storage; distinct hardware revision from the MalDuino Elite already tracked.

name: MalDuino W
one_line: WiFi-controlled BadUSB device: run/edit/delete/download keystroke-injection scripts over a web interface instead of reprogramming via cable. Converted from GBP 49 at ~1.354 USD/GBP.
why_notable: Wireless variant of the MalDuino line letting an operator trigger payloads remotely over WiFi rather than needing physical reprogramming access.

name: WiFi Deauther
one_line: ESP8266-based standalone device that sends 802.11 deauthentication frames to disconnect clients from a WiFi network, plus beacon and probe-request spamming, controlled via a web UI. Converted from GBP 37 at ~1.354 USD/GBP.
why_notable: Purpose-built, cased deauth/beacon-spam tool distinct from the DSTIKE Deauther Watch and generic Deauth Detector already tracked.

name: FlatSat – DEFCON 34
one_line: RP2040-based training board preloaded with intentionally vulnerable firmware mimicking spacecraft systems, for practicing binary exploitation, SWD/UART hardware attacks, and LoRa telemetry analysis with an SDR.
why_notable: Purpose-built satellite-cybersecurity CTF hardware target presented at DEF CON 34; currently out of stock but a real catalog item with a listed price.

name: Minino – DEFCON 34
one_line: DEF CON 34 commemorative edition of the ESP32-S3 Minino BLE/WiFi IoT security multitool.
why_notable: Same Minino platform already tracked, sold as a DEFCON-branded hardware edition under a different listing name.

name: Minino – DEFCON 33
one_line: DEF CON 33 commemorative edition of the ESP32-S3 Minino BLE/WiFi IoT security multitool.
why_notable: Same Minino platform already tracked, sold as a prior-year DEFCON-branded hardware edition.

name: Badge HackGDL
one_line: Official Hack GDL 2025 conference badge built on the Minino BLE/WiFi platform (ESP32-S3, OLED), running the same firmware apps as Minino.
why_notable: Conference badge that is functionally a Minino variant, worth flagging as a possible duplicate rather than a distinct device.

name: Faulty Cat V2.2
one_line: Portable EMFI (electromagnetic fault injection) glitcher for bypassing chip security and extracting firmware/credentials.
why_notable: Versioned revision of the already-tracked Faulty Cat glitching tool; likely the same device line under a version-numbered listing.

name: Flipper Add-On: CANBus
one_line: Flipper Zero GPIO add-on board for sniffing and injecting CAN bus traffic, with OBD2 scanning and UDS diagnostics on authorized vehicles.
why_notable: Adds automotive CAN bus sniff/inject/OBD2 capability to the Flipper Zero, a capability not covered by any existing Flipper add-on in the database.

name: Flipper Add-On: Marauder_Spoof
one_line: Flipper Zero GPIO add-on board running ESP32 Marauder firmware with added WiFi/BLE spoofing hardware.
why_notable: Flipper-form-factor ESP32 Marauder board, distinct SKU from Electronic Cats' plain Marauder add-on.

name: Flipper Add-On: Marauder
one_line: Flipper Zero GPIO add-on board running ESP32 Marauder firmware for WiFi/BLE scanning, deauth, and packet capture.
why_notable: Gives the Flipper Zero ESP32 Marauder WiFi/BLE audit capability via a dedicated add-on board.

name: Flipper Add-On: Ethernet
one_line: ENC28J60-based Flipper Zero add-on board for wired-LAN ARP scanning, LLDP passive discovery, and packet sniffing over Ethernet.
why_notable: Gives the Flipper Zero wired-network auditing capability it does not have natively.

name: Flipper Add-On: MagSpoof
one_line: Flipper Zero GPIO add-on board implementing the MagSpoof magnetic-stripe emulator/spoofer technique.
why_notable: Flipper-specific hardware implementation of the MagSpoof magstripe-emulation technique already tracked as a standalone device elsewhere.

name: Flipper Add-on SubGhz
one_line: Flipper Zero GPIO add-on board extending sub-GHz (CC1101-class) radio capability.
why_notable: Third-party sub-GHz extension board for the Flipper Zero from a known hardware-security vendor.

name: Flipper Add-On: Modbus
one_line: RS485/Modbus Flipper Zero GPIO add-on board for interacting with industrial control protocols.
why_notable: Rare industrial-control-systems (ICS/Modbus) testing add-on for the Flipper Zero platform.

name: MagSpoof V4
one_line: Wireless magnetic-stripe emulator device that transmits card data without swiping, sold at a discounted price from $18.
why_notable: Likely the same MagSpoof device family already tracked under the generic name, sold here as a specific hardware revision.

name: MagSpoof V5
one_line: Current-generation wireless magnetic-stripe emulator; listing shows a price range of $35-$100 depending on configuration.
why_notable: Newest hardware revision of the MagSpoof device family already tracked under the generic name.

name: PAW Protector
one_line: Inline USB-A adapter that blocks the data lines on a USB connection while passing 2.4A fast charging, to prevent juice-jacking on public USB ports.
why_notable: Defensive USB data-blocker device purpose-built against malicious public charging ports/cables.

name: Paw Detector – Malicious USB cables detector
one_line: Pocket USB-A adapter with an LED that lights steadily if a plugged-in cable contains a hidden keylogger or data-exfiltration circuit.
why_notable: Standalone hardware tool for detecting malicious/keylogging USB cables before use, presented at DEF CON 34.

name: HiLetgo PN532 NFC NXP RFID Module V3 Kit
one_line: PN532-chipset NFC/RFID reader-writer breakout board (I2C/SPI/HSU) that can read, write, and emulate 13.56MHz tags, used with libnfc/Arduino/Raspberry Pi.
why_notable: The PN532 chipset is the most widely used NFC controller in DIY/security tooling (libnfc-compatible, used in many RFID projects); this is a common low-cost breakout of it. Corroborated as a well-known module type via Adafruit's own PN532 breakout documentation, independent of this marketplace listing.

name: 2 PCS CC1101 Module with SMA Antenna Transceiver Module (433/315/868/915MHz)
one_line: CC1101-chipset sub-GHz transceiver breakout board with SMA antenna, tunable across 300-348/387-464/779-928MHz, sold as a 2-pack.
why_notable: CC1101 external modules are one of the most common third-party sub-GHz accessories for Flipper Zero/Arduino sub-GHz replay and range-extension projects, corroborated by multiple independent (Tindie, blog) sources beyond this marketplace listing.

name: 13.56MHz RFID Field Strength Meter
one_line: Passive, battery-free handheld meter that measures 13.56MHz RFID field strength for ISO-calibrated accuracy testing.
why_notable: Purpose-built RFID field-strength measurement tool, a device type not currently represented in the database.

name: Alfa AWUS036ACHM
one_line: USB WiFi adapter with Linux in-kernel monitor-mode and packet-injection support, widely used for WiFi pentesting.
why_notable: Alfa's monitor-mode/injection-capable adapters are a longstanding staple of WiFi penetration testing kits and are not currently represented in the database.

name: ARD RFID Blocker (Pack of 2) - NFC Blocker
one_line: Credit-card-sized, battery-free active RFID/NFC jammer that blocks reads of cards placed above or below it, unlike passive faraday-cage sleeves.
why_notable: Active (not merely shielding) RFID/NFC jamming device, distinct from passive blocking wallets.

name: AWOK Dual C5 Touch
one_line: Dual-band WiFi 6 and BLE wardriving touchscreen accessory board for Flipper Zero.
why_notable: Possible successor/variant of the AWOK Dual Touch v3 already tracked; flagged for review rather than treated as identical.

name: BugBlat miniSniffer 2
one_line: Compact, cross-platform hardware USB protocol analyzer for capturing and debugging USB traffic.
why_notable: Dedicated USB protocol-analysis hardware distinct from the Cynthion/Facedancer/GreatFET tools already tracked.

name: Chameleon Lite
one_line: Low-cost HF/MIFARE RFID emulator specialized for high-frequency card emulation, successor to the discontinued ChameleonMini/Tiny line.
why_notable: Current-generation entry-level Chameleon RFID emulator not covered by the Tiny, RevG, or Ultra models already tracked.

name: Chameleon Ultra DevKit
one_line: Chameleon Ultra RFID emulator variant with exposed headers for flashing, debugging, and expansion.
why_notable: Same Chameleon Ultra platform already tracked, sold as a developer-focused hardware variant.

name: ChipWhisperer - HuskyPlus
one_line: Side-channel analysis and fault-injection platform, an upgraded model above the existing ChipWhisperer-Husky.
why_notable: Higher-end successor to the ChipWhisperer-Husky already tracked, now in scope under the professional-gear price allowance.

name: Dual Mode Paxton Long Range / Stealth Decoy Reader
one_line: Long-range (up to 10cm) RFID skimmer targeting Paxton access-control readers, manageable and analyzable from a phone with Proxmark cloning support.
why_notable: Described by the seller as the first publicly available long-range Paxton-specific RFID skimmer; a notable physical-access-testing device.

name: iCS Decoder for iCLASS SE/SEOS Decoder
one_line: Add-on decoder module for the iCopy-X that decodes and clones iCLASS SE and iCLASS SEOS access-control badges.
why_notable: Seller describes it as the only device capable of cloning/decoding iCLASS SE/SEOS badges, a notable capability gap-filler for RFID pentesting.

name: Industrial Handheld UHF Reader
one_line: Handheld UHF RFID reader built to work with UHFKill for locating and confirming deactivation of embedded UHF tags.
why_notable: Professional-grade UHF RFID tooling above $1,000, now explicitly in scope; complements the UHFKill deactivation tool.

name: Feberis Pro
one_line: RF pentesting accessory board for Flipper Zero adding boosted RF, WiFi, BLE, IoT-protocol and GPS capability.
why_notable: Multi-radio Flipper Zero accessory bundling several capabilities the base Flipper lacks or has only weakly.

name: DigiLab for FlipperZero
one_line: Flipper Zero accessory for probing digital electronics: reads voltages, signals, and protocol traffic directly.
why_notable: General-purpose digital signal exploration accessory for the Flipper Zero not covered by existing GPIO add-ons.

name: GhostBoard
one_line: Flipper Zero accessory board running the Ghost ESP firmware for WiFi 6 and BLE 5 auditing.
why_notable: Commercial Flipper-specific hardware implementation of the Ghost ESP audit suite already represented generically in the database as a bare ESP32 board.

name: Glytch Ethernet Module for Pineapple Pager
one_line: Add-on module giving the WiFi Pineapple Pager wired Ethernet connectivity for LAN-based payloads.
why_notable: Capability-adding accessory for the already-tracked WiFi Pineapple Pager, enabling wired-network attack payloads.

name: Glytch GPS Module for Pineapple Pager
one_line: Add-on module giving the WiFi Pineapple Pager GPS for geo-coded wardriving and WiGLE-compatible logging.
why_notable: Capability-adding accessory for the already-tracked WiFi Pineapple Pager, enabling location-tagged wardriving.

name: Glytch Mesh Module for Pineapple Pager
one_line: Add-on module giving the WiFi Pineapple Pager decentralized LoRa mesh messaging.
why_notable: Capability-adding accessory for the already-tracked WiFi Pineapple Pager; mesh comms rather than direct offensive/defensive capability, hence borderline.

name: I2CDriver
one_line: Standalone I2C bus debug/development tool with an onboard screen for real-time visual feedback while developing or flashing I2C devices.
why_notable: Widely used hardware-hacking bus tool for I2C interaction/debugging, distinct from the Bus Pirate and Glasgow tools already tracked.

name: IR Blaster
one_line: Flipper Zero accessory with seven high-intensity LEDs to extend infrared/remote-control range.
why_notable: Third-party IR range-boost accessory for the Flipper Zero; may overlap functionally with the already-tracked Rabbit-Labs Slim Shady IR Blaster.

name: MastaBlasta - IR Blaster
one_line: Long-range infrared blaster accessory for the Flipper Zero.
why_notable: Another third-party IR range-boost accessory for the Flipper Zero; likely overlaps with the already-tracked Slim Shady IR Blaster and the Lab401 house-brand IR Blaster above.

name: KIISU - Compact Flipper alternative
one_line: Credit-card-sized, budget Flipper Zero alternative compatible with Flipper firmware, software and add-ons.
why_notable: Likely the same KIISU device family already tracked as KIISU V4B, listed here under a plain name.

name: Kronos Electric Pick
one_line: Motorized electric lock-pick gun with adjustable amplitude, powered rather than a purely manual pick.
why_notable: Unlike purely mechanical lockpicks (out of scope), this is a powered/electronic pick gun; flagged for a scope judgment call.

name: Long Range RFID Reader / Writer DL533N XL
one_line: LibNFC-compatible HF RFID reader/writer/sniffer/emulator that reads MIFARE Classic/Ultralight/DESFire/FeliCa/NTAG tags from up to 18cm away, designed to be hidden under tables or in bags.
why_notable: Long-range covert HF RFID reading device for physical penetration testing, distinct from handheld cloning tools already tracked.

name: Long-range iCLASS RFID Capture System
one_line: Long-range (up to 45cm) iCLASS RFID skimmer, managed from a phone, with wireless cloning via Proxmark.
why_notable: Professional-grade long-range iCLASS skimming hardware above $1,000-tier pricing, now explicitly in scope.

name: Long-range MaxiProx 5375 125KHz Capture System
one_line: Long-range (up to 60cm) 125kHz RFID skimmer built on the HID MaxiProx reader, managed from a phone with Proxmark cloning support.
why_notable: Professional long-range low-frequency RFID skimming hardware, a distinct capability tier from handheld cloners.

name: MACOBOX - Hardware Pentest Platform
one_line: Complete hardware penetration testing platform for rapid configuration, connection, and firmware dumping/analysis across multiple hardware interfaces.
why_notable: High-end professional hardware-hacking platform, now explicitly in scope under the >$1,000 professional-gear allowance; vendor/specs need further research before a full record is written.

name: NanoVNA-F
one_line: Portable vector network analyzer for measuring and tuning antenna setups (SWR, impedance).
why_notable: General-purpose RF test instrument widely used in the SDR/RF hacking community for antenna work; flagged borderline since it is not itself an offensive/defensive security tool.

name: NFCKill (Professional Version)
one_line: Device that destroys RFID tags and tests RFID hardware failure modes/fire-compliance, and can disable embedded RFID stickers.
why_notable: Likely the same NFCKill product family already tracked as NFC Kill (v3), sold here under a differently named version.

name: O.MG Adapter Elite
one_line: O.MG payload-injection platform with wireless control embedded in a USB-A to USB-C OTG adapter.
why_notable: Same O.MG platform already tracked as O.MG Adapter, sold here as a higher-end 'Elite' variant.

name: O.MG Cable Programmer (USB A+C)
one_line: Programming/flashing tool for configuring O.MG Cable devices.
why_notable: Support tool for the already-tracked O.MG Cable line; included for completeness though it is an accessory rather than an attack device itself.

name: O.MG Malicious Cable Detector
one_line: Handheld device for detecting malicious USB cables (e.g. O.MG-style implants) before use.
why_notable: Defensive counterpart to the O.MG Cable attack platform, distinct from Electronic Cats' Paw Detector.

name: PandwaRF Marauder
one_line: Autonomous covert RF/remote-control signal capture ('dead-drop') device integrating with the PandwaRF ecosystem for rolling/fixed-code analysis, decryption and generation.
why_notable: High-end professional sub-GHz signals-intelligence device above $1,000, now explicitly in scope; distinct from the already-tracked PandwaRF Rogue Pro.

name: PiKVM v4 Plus - Hardware RAT
one_line: KVM-over-IP hardware remote access tool with built-in cellular (3/4/5G) connectivity, marketed for covert drop-in red-team installs.
why_notable: Repurposes KVM-over-IP hardware as a covert, network-independent remote-access implant for red-team engagements.

name: PortaPack H4M Pro
one_line: All-in-one portable SDR built on a HackRF Pro with a PortaPack H4M display/interface for 100kHz-6GHz capture, analysis and replay.
why_notable: Likely a 'Pro' hardware revision of the HackRF + PortaPack H4M combination already tracked.

name: Project Reboot: Hardware Audit Training Target
one_line: Progressive hardware-hacking training board with staged UART, SPI, I2C and Bluetooth challenges.
why_notable: Dedicated training/CTF target for practicing hardware-hacking bus attacks, comparable in purpose to FlatSat but general-purpose rather than satellite-themed.

name: Proxmark 3 RDV4 - BlueShark Standalone Module
one_line: Bluetooth add-on module for the Proxmark 3 RDV4 enabling standalone/wireless operation.
why_notable: Capability-adding accessory for the already-tracked Proxmark3 RDV4.01, giving it wireless standalone operation.

name: Proxmark 3 RDV4 - SIM/SAM Extension
one_line: SIM/SAM card slot extension module for the Proxmark 3 RDV4, enabling smart-card cryptographic operations.
why_notable: Capability-adding accessory for the already-tracked Proxmark3 RDV4.01, adding smart-card crypto support.

name: Proxmark 5 - Wireless + Battery Module
one_line: Drop-in wireless and battery module for the Proxmark 5, enabling untethered mobile RFID pentesting.
why_notable: Capability-adding accessory for the already-tracked Proxmark 5, enabling wireless mobile operation.

name: RFID Field Detector Ultra - LF/HF/UHF
one_line: Passive, battery-free tri-band (LF/HF/UHF) detector that identifies the presence of RFID reader fields.
why_notable: Tri-band RFID field detector distinct from the single-band 13.56MHz Field Strength Meter also found at this shop; useful for identifying covert readers.

name: SPIDriver
one_line: Standalone SPI bus debug/development tool with an onboard screen for real-time visual feedback while developing or flashing SPI devices.
why_notable: Hardware-hacking bus tool for SPI interaction/debugging, complementing the I2CDriver from the same maker.

name: Stealth Decoy Reader
one_line: Rapidly deployable, undetectable decoy RFID/PIN-pad reader that captures credentials, managed and analyzed from a phone.
why_notable: Base-model covert credential-harvesting decoy reader; the Paxton and long-range variants at this shop build on this platform.

name: TermDriver 2
one_line: USB-to-serial adapter with an onboard screen for real-time debugging of serial connections and monitoring headless systems.
why_notable: General serial-debug hardware tool sold alongside I2CDriver/SPIDriver at hardware-hacking shops; borderline since it is not offense/defense-specific by itself.

name: TinySA Ultra+
one_line: Handheld RF spectrum analyzer for identifying and locating transmitting devices/signals.
why_notable: General-purpose spectrum analyzer widely used in the SDR/RF hacking community for signal identification; borderline since it is general RF test equipment rather than an offense/defense tool per se.

name: UHFKill
one_line: Handheld device that wirelessly and permanently disables UHF RFID tags embedded in clothing, shoes, or other products.
why_notable: Described by the seller as the only publicly available UHF RFID deactivation tool; professional-grade device now explicitly in scope above $1,000.

name: USB RFID Reader/Writer DL533N
one_line: 13.56MHz LibNFC-compatible RFID reader/writer in a USB-stick form factor: read, write, crack, dump, modify and emulate tags.
why_notable: Compact USB-stick RFID reader/writer distinct from the longer-range DL533N XL variant at the same shop.
